comments.author: @hillbilly4christ638
comments.text: I lived there for a year and a half.  I believe the reason why they live so long is because they eat so much fresh food.  There are markets everywhere and people buy fresh virtually everyday and they consume a lot of seafood.

comments.author: @TravelBeyond4K
comments.text: The nature shots of these hidden tropical islands are something else. Makes you really want to travel there and see what life in Okinawa is like.

comments.author: @Abdul-e3m
comments.text: Uchinā (what you call Okinawa) was stolen by the Japanese and is co occupied by them and the US military and one day it will be free of Japan and America.

comments.author: @JapanTravelLifestyle
comments.text: Beautiful video, thank you for sharing it. I really liked how you connected the slower pace of Okinawa with community and everyday human connection, not just the scenery. I’ve been looking into the happiness and community side of life there, so this was especially interesting to watch.

comments.author: @mariela2826
comments.text: Okinawa is so beautiful! It’s people have western features! High cheech bones and big eyes, Nice eyebrows. They clear the Jomon people descendants that uses to live from Hokkaido to Okinawa. Lots of secrets in Okinawa about the Jomon.

replies.author: @BestTravel2
replies.text: It’s fascinating to learn about the historical roots and the unique cultural identity of the people here!

comments.text: I’m an Okinawan and still live in Okinawa. Some of the visuals and information are incorrect.

comments.author: @jayjayperez-v4i
comments.text: Am I the only one who feels this way? I just don’t really like  ai generated documentaries they don’t feel natural to me and somehow they just feel different.I much prefer documentaries that feel more authentic and real.

comments.author: @YOU-c4b5f
comments.text:
Okinawa has a wonderful phrase: "Ichariba Choodee." It means, "Once we meet, we are brothers."
As an Okinawan, I truly love this spirit that embraces peace.
Please, everyone—come to Okinawa!

replies.author: @BestTravel2
replies.text: It truly feels like a refreshing paradise, doesn't it?
